elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; there is no commercial general liability requirement anywhere in the rendered text (18.14 concerns counterparts and language only).

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit appears; the insertion states only 'errors and omissions insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.'

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted E&O limit is 'not less than USD 1,000,000', below the preferred USD 2,000,000 threshold.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The drafter's own insertion requires cyber and privacy cover, indicating the data-processing condition is treated as applicable, but the limit is 'not less than USD 2,000,000', short of USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation obligation is included in the inserted Insurance paragraph or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no certificate-of-insurance delivery mechanic; the rationale expressly leaves certificates out of scope.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 'Array shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000' — an affirmative, unconditional covenant on the counterparty at the required floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: '... and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000' — matches the fallback amount and the required cyber/privacy category.

reasons: Finding classification 'missing' is supported: the rendered original (18.14 Counterparts; Other Matters) and the cited context contain no insurance covenant, only unrelated freight/health-insurance references inside Net Sales; insertion is the correct remedy.

The fallback checklist is complete on its face: both atomic elements (E&O ≥ USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy ≥ USD 2,000,000) are expressed as unconditional 'shall maintain' obligations of the counterparty at or above the stated floors, so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level.

Preferred level is not reached — CGL per-occurrence and aggregate limits, the USD 2,000,000 E&O limit, the USD 5,000,000 cyber limit, workers' compensation and certificates on request are all absent. That is a deliberate fallback target and is acceptable, but the redline should not be described as meeting the preferred position.

Minimality holds: the insertion adds only the two fallback coverages and omits model-language extras (no 'at its own expense', no term-plus-one-year survival tail, no certificate procedure, no CGL). No existing words were deleted or paraphrased, and no favourable retained language was disturbed.

Intent preserved: the counterparts, electronic-signature and English-language provisions of 18.14 survive intact; the new covenant creates no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradiction with Article 16 indemnities, which it supports.

Drafting nit only (not a deviation): the new 'Insurance.' paragraph is appended after 18.14 without its own section number — give it a discrete number (e.g. 18.15) so it does not read as part of the Counterparts clause. Optionally consider adding a duration ('throughout the Term') for enforceability, though no selected element requires it.
